$comment: Editorial one-line descriptions of works, merged into each work's manifest at sync time
by scripts/sync-corpus.mjs, and rendered by /documents (and anywhere else reading
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS RATHER THAN A FIELD IN corpus/works/*/manifest.json: those manifests
are GENERATED. A re-parse rewrites them, so a description written there survives exactly
until the next parser fix — and this project fixes parsers by re-parsing (see CLAUDE.md's
're-parse, never re-crawl'). Descriptions are editorial, not scraped, so they live in
tracked source and are merged in on the way to the site. The corpus stays purely generated
and re-parsing stays free of consequences. Same posture, same reasoning, and the same place
HOW A DESCRIPTION IS WRITTEN — the rule is not negotiable, and it is the whole point:
a description is derived from READING THE DOCUMENT IN THE CORPUS, never from recollection
of what a document with that title probably says. See docs/writing-descriptions.md for the
procedure and for why a plausible-sounding wrong description is worse than none.
Keyed by work id, so the two language editions of one document are described separately —
a description is prose in a particular language, not a translated label. A work with no
entry here simply has no description; nothing renders a placeholder.

descriptions.encyclical.acerbo-nimis.en: Pius X's encyclical on the neglect of religious instruction, arguing that widespread ignorance of Christian doctrine — even among the educated — is the root of moral decline, and that teaching it is a pastor's first duty under the Council of Trent. It closes with six binding ordinances: weekly catechism for children, First Communion preparation, a parish Confraternity of Christian Doctrine, and adult instruction on holy days.
descriptions.encyclical.ad-beatissimi-apostolorum.en: Benedict XV's first encyclical, issued three months into the First World War, appeals for an end to the fighting and traces its underlying causes to a decline in mutual charity, contempt for authority, and class conflict between rich and poor, naming love of money as their deepest root. It also calls on Catholics to abandon factional labels and remain united with their bishops, then closes with a prayer for peace.
descriptions.encyclical.ad-petri.en: John XXIII's first encyclical, written at the start of his pontificate around the recognition of truth, “a renewal of Christian morals,” and “a restoration of unity, harmony, and peace.” It addresses truth against error and the press's duties, unity among nations, within the family, and within the Church around the newly announced Ecumenical Council, then counsels bishops, clergy, religious, and the sick.
descriptions.encyclical.ad-petri.pt: Primeira carta encíclica de João XXIII, dirigida a todo o orbe católico, sobre o conhecimento da verdade, a restauração da unidade e da paz na caridade. Trata da verdade e do indiferentismo religioso, da concórdia entre povos, classes e famílias, da unidade da Igreja em torno da Cátedra de Pedro, e encerra com exortações paternais a bispos, clero, religiosos, missionários, pobres, refugiados e à Igreja perseguida.
descriptions.encyclical.adiutricem.en: Leo XIII's encyclical urging Catholics to devote the month of October to the Rosary, presenting it as the most effective prayer for the object then closest to his heart: the reconciliation of nations separated from the Church, above all in the Christian East. He recounts Mary's historic role as guardian of Church unity, from Dominic Guzman's preaching to earlier popes' efforts to spread the devotion in the East.
descriptions.encyclical.adiutricem.pt: Carta encíclica de Leão XIII sobre o Rosário como via de retorno à unidade da Igreja. Pede orações perseverantes pela reconciliação dos povos separados do Oriente e do Ocidente, apresenta Maria — evocando o Concílio de Éfeso — como o vínculo capaz de reuni-los sob o Pontífice Romano, e anuncia a construção de um templo à Rainha do Rosário em Patras.
descriptions.encyclical.aeterni-patris.en: Argues that the restoration of Christian, especially Scholastic, philosophy is needed in Catholic schools, tracing the errors unsettling civil and public life to false philosophical teaching, and holding up Thomas Aquinas's synthesis — inherited from the Fathers and taught at Paris, Salamanca, and Louvain — as the surest defense of the faith and remedy for those errors.
descriptions.encyclical.arcanum.en: Leo XIII's encyclical on Christian marriage: Christ raised it to a sacrament and restored the unity and indissolubility it had lost, so the Church holds authority over the marriages of the baptized. It argues against treating marriage as a merely civil contract subject to the state, sets out the evils that follow from divorce, and closes commending to the bishops those living outside a lawful bond.
descriptions.encyclical.caritas-in-veritate.en: Benedict XVI's encyclical on integral human development in charity and truth, revisiting Paul VI's Populorum Progressio more than forty years after its publication. Across six chapters it treats globalization, human rights and duties, the environment, international cooperation, and technology, arguing that authentic development needs gratuitousness, openness to life and the logic of gift alongside justice.
descriptions.encyclical.casti-connubii.en: Pius XI's encyclical on Christian marriage, organized around St. Augustine's three blessings of wedlock — offspring, conjugal faith, and the sacrament — expounding each in turn before cataloguing the errors attacking them: contraception, abortion, eugenic sterilization, divorce, and the “false emancipation” of women, and closing with remedies for restoring marriage to the divine plan.
descriptions.encyclical.communium-rerum.en: Pius X marks the eighth centenary of the death of St. Anselm of Canterbury, praising his sanctity and his stand for the Church's liberty against secular encroachment, then holds him up as founder of a scholastic middle way between rationalist excess and fideist neglect — deployed as a direct warning against modernist "agnosticism" and dialecticians who overreach reason's limits.
descriptions.encyclical.depuis-le-jour.en: Leo XIII's encyclical to the bishops and clergy of France on forming priests. It sets a curriculum: classical letters for junior seminaries, then rational philosophy grounded in Aeterni Patris against modern errors, scholastic theology built on St. Thomas's Summa, the Roman Catechism, Scripture, Church history and canon law for senior ones — then turns to ordained priests, urging obedience to their bishops and zeal tempered by prudence.
descriptions.encyclical.deus-caritas-est.pt: Trata do amor cristão a partir de « Deus é amor » (1 Jo 4, 16): a primeira parte busca a unidade entre eros e agape na criação e na história da salvação, culminando no amor a Deus e ao próximo revelados em Jesus Cristo; a segunda volta-se para a caritas como prática da Igreja enquanto « comunidade de amor », discutindo justiça, caridade e seus responsáveis.
descriptions.encyclical.dilexit-nos.en: Francis's 2024 encyclical on devotion to the Sacred Heart of Jesus: what the symbol of the 'heart' can still mean for a distracted age, what Christ's own gaze, words and pierced side reveal about his human and divine love, the history of this devotion from Margaret Mary through Francis de Sales, Claude de la Colombière, Charles de Foucauld and Thérèse of Lisieux, and how reparation for love unreturned extends into fraternity, mission and social concern.
descriptions.encyclical.divini-redemptoris.en: Pius XI's encyclical on atheistic communism, written as its persecution intensified in Russia, Mexico and Spain. It traces communism's Marxist materialism, how it strips man of liberty and dignity and would dissolve family and property into a collectivity built for production, opposes to it the Church's teaching on God, man and society, and prescribes remedies — renewed Christian life, social justice, Catholic Action — under St. Joseph's protection.
descriptions.encyclical.divini-redemptoris.pt: Carta encíclica de Pio XI sobre o comunismo ateu, escrita quando a sua perseguição já lavrava na Rússia, no México e na Espanha. Expõe a doutrina comunista e o seu materialismo marxista, com frutos deploráveis como a luta contra tudo o que se chama Deus e o terrorismo, opondo-lhe a doutrina católica sobre Deus, o homem e a sociedade, e indicando remédios: renovação da vida cristã, justiça social e Ação Católica.
descriptions.encyclical.ecclesiam.en: Paul VI's first encyclical, written one year into his pontificate as a statement of governing priorities: the Church's need for deeper self-awareness, the renewal called for by the Second Vatican Council, and dialogue with the world. The final and longest part elaborates dialogue as method, extending it outward through concentric circles — from all mankind, to believers in one God, to other Christians, to Catholics themselves.
descriptions.encyclical.editae-saepe.en: Marking the third centenary of St. Charles Borromeo's canonization, Pius X holds him up as the model of true reform: fidelity to Rome and self-effacing zeal against heresy, opposed both to the Protestant revolt Borromeo fought and to what Pius calls the apostasy of his own day. It contrasts the true reformer, who trusts God and the Church, with the false one, who seeks his own glory, closing with an appeal to Catholic Action.
descriptions.encyclical.evangelium-vitae.pt: Sobre o valor da vida humana e a sua inviolabilidade, diante das novas ameaças do aborto e da eutanásia: parte do grito do sangue de Abel e do eclipse do sentido da vida, percorre o mandamento «não matarás» perante a lei civil e a lei moral, e chama a uma nova cultura da vida, terminando com uma prece a Maria, Mãe dos viventes.
descriptions.encyclical.fratelli-tutti.pt: Carta encíclica de Francisco sobre a fraternidade e a amizade social, inspirada no apelo de São Francisco de Assis, de quem toma o título. Parte da parábola do bom samaritano para denunciar as sombras dum mundo fechado e propor a política melhor, o diálogo e a amizade social, e o papel das religiões ao serviço da fraternidade no mundo.
descriptions.encyclical.haurietis-aquas.pt: Carta encíclica de Pio XII sobre o culto ao Sagrado Coração de Jesus, escrita para o centenário da instituição da festa por Pio IX. Percorre os fundamentos desse culto nas Escrituras do Antigo e do Novo Testamento, na tradição dos Padres e no seu desenvolvimento histórico até à Idade Média, e conclui exortando os fiéis a praticá-lo com maior fervor.
descriptions.encyclical.humanae-vitae.pt: Carta encíclica de Paulo VI sobre a regulação da natalidade. Reafirma a ligação inseparável entre união e procriação no ato conjugal, defende a paternidade responsável e exclui como ilícitos o aborto, a esterilização direta e os métodos artificiais de contracepção, admitindo apenas o recurso aos períodos infecundos. Termina com apelos aos governantes, cientistas, esposos, médicos, sacerdotes e bispos.
descriptions.encyclical.humanum-genus.en: Leo XIII's encyclical on Freemasonry, framing history as a struggle between two opposed kingdoms and naming Freemasonry as the organizing centre of a wider network of secret societies. It traces their doctrine to naturalism and the denial of revelation, which it holds corrodes marriage, education and civil authority, and prescribes religious instruction, the revival of workers' guilds, and the Third Order of St. Francis.
descriptions.encyclical.humanum-genus.pt: Carta encíclica de Leão XIII sobre a Maçonaria, que apresenta a história como luta entre duas cidades opostas — a terrena e a celestial — e identifica a seita dos maçons como centro de uma rede de sociedades secretas. Atribui a sua doutrina ao naturalismo, que corrompe o casamento, a educação e a autoridade civil, e propõe remédios: instrução religiosa, associações de trabalhadores e a Ordem Terceira de São Francisco.
descriptions.encyclical.immortale-dei.en: Leo XIII's encyclical on the Christian constitution of states: civil authority comes from God, not from the sovereignty of the people, and is bound to honor religion publicly. Rejecting the naturalist doctrines that exclude God from public life, it sets out the concord due between Church and State, and closes urging Catholics to take an active part in public affairs despite lawful disagreement over forms of government.
descriptions.encyclical.immortale-dei.pt: Carta encíclica de Leão XIII sobre a constituição cristã dos Estados: defende que o poder público só pode vir de Deus, expõe a Igreja como sociedade perfeita e soberana na sua esfera própria, distinta mas harmónica com o poder civil, refuta a tese liberal de separar os negócios da Igreja dos do Estado, e conclui exortando os católicos à unidade na participação da vida política.
descriptions.encyclical.laudato-si.en: Francis's encyclical on ecology, taking its title from Saint Francis's Canticle of the Creatures. It diagnoses pollution, climate change, water scarcity, biodiversity loss and social breakdown as symptoms of one crisis rooted in a 'technocratic paradigm,' develops an 'integral ecology' linking care for nature to justice for the poor, and proposes lines of dialogue, education, and 'ecological conversion.'
descriptions.encyclical.laudato-si.pt: Carta encíclica de Francisco, dirigida a cada pessoa que habita este planeta, sobre o cuidado da casa comum. Parte do diagnóstico do que está a acontecer à Terra — poluição, mudanças climáticas, perda de biodiversidade, desigualdade — para propor uma ecologia integral que una a questão ambiental à justiça social, recusando o paradigma tecnocrático e convidando à conversão ecológica; termina com duas orações.
descriptions.encyclical.libertas.en: Leo XIII's encyclical on the nature of human liberty, arguing true freedom lies in the will's conformity to the eternal law of God, not in acting simply as one pleases. It examines and limits the liberties liberalism champions — of worship, of speech and the press, of teaching, and of conscience — rejects unconditional separation of Church and State, and allows that Catholics may licitly prefer democratic government.
descriptions.encyclical.magnifica-humanitas.en: Leo XIV's encyclical on artificial intelligence and the social doctrine of the Church. Framed by two biblical images of collective building — the Tower of Babel and Nehemiah's rebuilding of Jerusalem — it argues that AI is not one more subject for social doctrine to address but a development that challenges its categories from within, and takes up human dignity and the common good, truth, work and freedom, and the growing place of autonomous systems in war.
descriptions.encyclical.magnifica-humanitas.pt: Carta encíclica de Leão XIV sobre a inteligência artificial e a doutrina social da Igreja. Estruturada em torno de duas imagens bíblicas da construção comum — a Torre de Babel e a reconstrução de Jerusalém por Neemias —, sustenta que a IA não é mais um tema a tratar pela doutrina social, mas um desenvolvimento que desafia as suas próprias categorias, e aborda a dignidade humana e o bem comum, a verdade, o trabalho e a liberdade, e o lugar crescente dos sistemas autónomos na guerra.
descriptions.encyclical.mediator-dei.en: The sacred liturgy as the public worship that the Church, united with Christ her divine Head, offers to God: the priesthood's role in the Eucharistic sacrifice, the laity's active yet real participation in it, the sacraments and sacramentals, the Divine Office and liturgical year, and pastoral counsel on sacred art, music and altar servers, warning against both careless innovation and an exaggerated antiquarian zeal for reviving ancient forms.
descriptions.encyclical.mortalium-animos.pt: Carta encíclica de Pio XI aos bispos católicos sobre a unidade verdadeira da religião, contra o movimento "pancristão" e seus congressos ecumênicos, que buscam uma fraternidade comum ignorando as diferenças doutrinárias. Pio XI ensina que só existe uma religião verdadeira, revelada por Deus e guardada pela Igreja Católica, e que a unidade dos cristãos só se dá pelo retorno dos dissidentes a essa única Igreja, em obediência ao Romano Pontífice.
descriptions.encyclical.mystici-corporis-christi.en: On the Church as the Mystical Body of Christ: a single visible Body with Christ as Head, animated by the Holy Spirit and built up through the sacraments and the juridical bonds of faith, hope and charity. It refutes rationalist, naturalist and mystical errors about the Church's nature and closes by entrusting her peace to the Virgin Mary.
descriptions.encyclical.mystici-corporis-christi.pt: Sobre o Corpo Místico de Cristo, que é a Igreja: define-a como um corpo único, visível e organicamente estruturado, cuja cabeça é Cristo e cujo vigário visível é o Papa, vivificada interiormente pelo Espírito Santo e unida pelos sacramentos, sobretudo a Eucaristia. Denuncia os erros do falso misticismo e do quietismo, exorta à caridade ativa para com a Igreja e encerra confiando os fiéis à Virgem Maria.
descriptions.encyclical.populorum.en: Paul VI's encyclical on the development of peoples, arguing that authentic development must be integral — of the whole man and of every man — and tracing the passage from less than human to more human conditions. It sets out the wealthier nations' threefold duty toward developing ones — solidarity, social justice and universal charity — and closes on development as the new name for peace.
descriptions.encyclical.populorum.pt: Carta encíclica de Paulo VI sobre o desenvolvimento dos povos, defendendo um desenvolvimento integral — do homem todo e de todos os homens — e a passagem de condições menos humanas, marcadas pela miséria e pela opressão, a condições mais humanas. Aponta o tríplice dever das nações ricas para com as mais pobres — solidariedade, justiça social e caridade universal — e conclui que o desenvolvimento é o novo nome da paz.
descriptions.encyclical.quadragesimo-anno.en: Pius XI's encyclical for the fortieth anniversary of Leo XIII's On the Condition of Workers, treated under three headings: that encyclical's fruits, Catholic teaching on property's individual and social character and on just wages, and a verdict on the present economic order — wealth concentrated into an “economic dictatorship,” free competition's self-destruction, and Socialism's irreconcilability with Christianity — closing with a call to restore society through vocational guilds and reform of morals.
descriptions.encyclical.quod-votis.en: Leo XIII writes to the Archbishops and Bishops of Austria — of Vienna, Wroclaw, Prague, and Krakow — approving their long-pending plan to found a Catholic university. He expresses joy that the project, awaited under his predecessors, is nearing completion, urges the faithful to hasten it, and directs that its final arrangements be reported to the Sacred Congregation of Studies for approval under canonical norms.
descriptions.encyclical.rerum-novarum.en: On the condition of labor amid industrial upheaval, addressing what the document itself calls the rights and duties of capital and labor. It refutes the socialist proposal to abolish private property, grounds ownership in natural and paternal right, sets out duties binding workers and employers alike, and turns to the roles of Church, State, and workingmen's associations in bettering the workman's condition.
descriptions.encyclical.rerum-novarum.pt: Encíclica de Leão XIII, de 1891, sobre a condição dos operários, escrita depois do fim das antigas corporações que os protegiam. Rejeita a solução socialista de abolir a propriedade particular como injusta, defende o direito natural à propriedade e à livre associação dos trabalhadores, e trata dos deveres do Estado, dos patrões e dos operários, incluindo a justa retribuição do trabalho.
descriptions.encyclical.singulari-quadam.en: Settles the German 'trade union controversy': whether Catholic workers, alongside purely Catholic Arbeitervereine, may join mixed interconfessional labor unions with Protestants. Addressed to Cardinal Kopp and the German bishops, it reaffirms Rerum Novarum's principles and permits qualified toleration of the Christian Trade Unions where local conditions warrant, provided members also belong to a Catholic association and the unions never act against Church teaching, under episcopal oversight.
descriptions.encyclical.spiritus-paraclitus.en: Benedict XV's encyclical marking the fifteenth centenary of St. Jerome's death, presenting his life and biblical scholarship as a model for the Church. Invoking Jerome's teaching, it restates the doctrine of the Bible's divine inspiration and total inerrancy against critics who deny it, particularly regarding the Gospels, and reaffirms Leo XIII's Providentissimus Deus, urging bishops to promote rigorous biblical study among seminarians and clergy.
descriptions.encyclical.veritatis-splendor.en: John Paul II's encyclical to the bishops on the foundations of Catholic moral theology, written amid dissent from the Church's moral teaching. Framed by Christ's dialogue with the rich young man — “Teacher, what good must I do to have eternal life?” — it treats freedom's dependence on truth and God's law, conscience, the moral act, and intrinsically evil acts, closing with an appeal to Mary, Mother of Mercy.
descriptions.vatii.dei-verbum.pt: Constituição dogmática do Concílio Vaticano II sobre a Revelação divina: como Deus se revela e se comunica ao homem em Cristo, a sua transmissão pela sagrada Tradição e pela Sagrada Escritura sob a vigilância do Magistério, a inspiração e a verdade dos livros do Antigo e do Novo Testamento, e o lugar da Escritura na vida, no estudo e na leitura da Igreja.
descriptions.vatii.dignitatis-humanae.en: Vatican II's declaration that the human person has a right to religious freedom: immunity from coercion, by individuals or government, in professing any religion, alone or in community. It argues the right rests first on human dignity and reason, then on revelation — since Christ invited faith rather than compelling it — and urges governments to secure it as a civil right within the bounds of just public order.
descriptions.vatii.dignitatis-humanae.pt: Declaração do Concílio Vaticano II sobre a liberdade religiosa: afirma que a pessoa humana tem direito à liberdade religiosa, entendida como imunidade de coacção em matéria religiosa, em privado e em público, só ou associada a outros. Expõe primeiro a doutrina geral, fundada na dignidade da pessoa humana e na razão, e depois mostra-a radicada na Revelação divina e no comportamento de Cristo e dos Apóstolos.
descriptions.vatii.gaudium-et-spes.en: The Church in the modern world, opening in solidarity with “the joys and the hopes, the griefs and the anxieties” of the age and addressed not only to the Church's own members but to the whole of humanity. Part I treats the dignity of the human person, human community, and human activity in the world; Part II takes up marriage and family, culture, economic and social life, the political community, and the fostering of peace among nations.
descriptions.vatii.gravissimum-educationis.en: Vatican II's declaration on Christian education, opening from every person's inalienable right to an education suited to their nature and final end. It sets out parents as the first educators, the Church's own role in forming the baptized, and the purpose of Catholic schools, colleges, universities and faculties of sacred sciences, closing with a call for coordination among Catholic educational institutions.
descriptions.vatii.gravissimum-educationis.pt: Declaração conciliar sobre a educação cristã, que parte do direito inalienável de todo o homem a uma educação correspondente à sua dignidade de pessoa. Afirma os pais como primeiros educadores, o papel próprio da Igreja na formação cristã dos baptizados, e a missão das escolas católicas, das universidades católicas e das faculdades de ciências sagradas, terminando com um apelo à coordenação entre as instituições escolares católicas.
descriptions.vatii.lumen-gentium.en: Vatican II's dogmatic constitution on the Church, describing it as sacrament and mystery of union with God, then as the People of God, structured by a hierarchy and episcopate in communion with the laity, called universally to holiness through varied vocations including the religious life, journeying toward its eschatological fulfillment, and inseparably bound to the Blessed Virgin Mary as Mother of God and image of the Church.
descriptions.vatii.lumen-gentium.pt: Constituição dogmática do Concílio Vaticano II sobre a Igreja, chamada luz dos povos e sacramento da união com Deus. Percorre o mistério da Igreja como povo de Deus e corpo de Cristo, sua constituição hierárquica de bispos, presbíteros e diáconos, a vocação dos leigos, o chamamento universal à santidade, a vida religiosa e a índole escatológica da Igreja peregrina, terminando com o lugar de Maria no mistério de Cristo e da Igreja.
descriptions.vatii.sacrosanctum-concilium.pt: Estabelece os princípios gerais da reforma e do incremento da Liturgia, pedindo a participação plena, consciente e activa dos fiéis nas celebrações. Organiza-se em capítulos sobre a Eucaristia, os demais sacramentos e sacramentais, o Ofício Divino, o ano litúrgico, a música sacra, e a arte sacra e as alfaias litúrgicas, com um apêndice sobre a revisão do calendário.
